boundary: Synthetic all-portfolio adaptive survival screen. It is not a calibrated empirical estimate and should not be treated as proof that any institutional portfolio would work in practice.

priors.empiricalBasis: Constraints on formal lobbying can shift influence to alternate venues and intermediaries; disclosure and sanctions help most when enforcement reaches those substitutes.
priors.modelUse: Anti-capture rows with audit, machine-readable logs, venue-shift detection, or sanctions reduce lobby adaptation and capture pressure; narrow caps and budget tools keep a substitution-risk caveat.

priors.empiricalBasis: Emergency abuse risk rises with long duration, weak sunsets, low judicial access, court backlogs, information control, and executive appointment or jurisdiction pressure.
priors.modelUse: Emergency-integrity rows reduce rights-threat inflow, court adaptation, court-curbing pressure, and review backlog only when review is fast, reason-giving, and anti-evasion oriented.

priors.empiricalBasis: Reform enactment and operational commencement should be separated; legality, staffing, data, transparency, and review capacity need to come before high-complexity redesigns.
priors.modelUse: Sequencing readiness reduces transition load, agency gaps, and delivery bottlenecks; complex one-shot redesigns carry higher transition and direct-evidence penalties.

priors.empiricalBasis: Implementation failure depends on intergovernmental conflict, capability shortfalls, demand-to-capacity pressure, and recovery speed, not a single generic capacity term.
priors.modelUse: The bridge now tracks federalism resistance, delivery bottleneck pressure, and recovery capacity separately before combining them into agency implementation gaps.

priors.empiricalBasis: Dissatisfaction is corrective only when citizens have credible voice, efficacy, fair procedures, and trusted intermediaries; trust erosion is faster than trust recovery.
priors.modelUse: Feedback correction capacity can turn backlash into alignment and policy correction, while weak voice causes faster legitimacy erosion.

priors.empiricalBasis: Hybrid and deliberative mechanisms are safer than standalone plebiscitary mechanisms; open participation without authentication or response duties can overload institutions or amplify capture.
priors.modelUse: Citizen assemblies, random public review panels, and comment-authenticity rules improve agenda correction; initiatives and petition channels also add rights-risk or overload pressure.

priors.empiricalBasis: Emergency review, audit/sanction regimes, participatory budgeting-style channels, and democracy vouchers have more direct evidence than pairwise amendment tournaments, portfolio-hybrid legislatures, or budgeted disclosed lobbying.
priors.modelUse: Low-direct-evidence families can rank highly synthetically, but the recommendation gate labels them as calibration gray-zone or do-not-recommend rather than provisional recommendations.

validationRequirements: Elicit score weights from an explicit loss function or stakeholder tradeoff exercise.
Backtest transition-load, agency-gap, voter-feedback, court-adaptation, and lobby-adaptation coefficients against historical reform episodes.
Use temporal holdouts and adversarial stress checks before treating any gate as decision-ready.
Require direct family-specific simulator work for pairwise, portfolio-hybrid, and budgeted-lobbying rows before recommending them.

baseline.label: Baseline
baseline.description: Default bridge coefficients with no additional stress modifiers.

high-capture-pressure.label: High Capture Pressure
high-capture-pressure.description: Organized interests adapt more aggressively, capture pressure starts higher, and capture controls are less effective.

low-public-trust.label: Low Public Trust
low-public-trust.description: Legitimacy and compliance start lower, and public-alignment losses have stronger legitimacy effects.

high-rights-threat.label: High Rights-Threat Environment
high-rights-threat.description: Bad-policy inflow is more likely to create rights-threatening review pressure.

court-curbing-noncompliance.label: Court-Curbing and Institutional Noncompliance Stress
court-curbing-noncompliance.description: Corrective review creates more retaliation pressure, institutional compliance falls, and court-curbing pressure decays slowly.

emergency-abuse-stress.label: Emergency Abuse Stress
emergency-abuse-stress.description: Emergency action and emergency litigation generate more rights-threatening policy, larger review dockets, and stronger legitimacy penalties when review cannot keep up.

administrative-complexity-stress.label: Administrative Overload and Complexity Stress
administrative-complexity-stress.description: Implementation is harder: effective complexity, delivery, review capacity, and compliance are reduced.

federalism-agency-capacity-stress.label: Federalism and Agency-Capacity Stress
federalism-agency-capacity-stress.description: Subnational resistance, agency undercapacity, procurement friction, and implementation bottlenecks weaken delivery, compliance, and correction capacity.
